clue.text: Pallid, sad type trembles, accepting what happens mostly

indicators.note: letters that tremble are shaken about and settle in a new order
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of that word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
a fact is something that is the case, what actually happens

explanation.surface: A pale, gloomy person shakes as they come to terms with events.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder trembling takes in FAC (FACT without its last letter) along with SAD TYPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasty-faced describes someone with an unhealthily pale complexion, the colour of uncooked pastry.

clue.text: See a cruiser in trouble round Australia? This may be called for (12, two words)

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the other piece, enclosing it
letters in trouble are thrown into disorder, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
A is an abbreviation for Australia, as in A$ for the Australian dollar

explanation.surface: A cruise ship in difficulties off Australia might need help to be summoned.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay half of the clue paints exactly the emergency the answer would be called out for.
explanation.definitionFit: An air-sea rescue is an operation using aircraft to save people in distress at sea, summoned in an emergency.

clue.text: Copper replacing inner parts of strong shelter

indicators.note: replacing the inner parts swaps out everything between the first and last letters

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
taken as written

explanation.surface: A policeman takes over the heart of a sturdy refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' invites a policeman; it is the metal, by its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Scug is a Scots and northern dialect word for a shelter or protection, also as a verb.

clue.text: It's given to Alzheimer's sufferer, certain for treatment

indicators.note: treatment works on something and changes it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A drug is sure to be prescribed to a patient with Alzheimer's disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacrine was the first drug licensed to treat Alzheimer's disease, a cholinesterase inhibitor.

clue.text: Dress with pedigree? It could cover embarrassment for many (7, two words)

definitions.text: It could cover embarrassment for many

parts.note: fig is dress or array, as in 'in full fig'
a family tree sets out a pedigree

explanation.surface: A posh frock with a family history could save many people's blushes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to Adam and Eve covering their nakedness with fig leaves; the tree supplies plenty of such cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Its large leaves are the traditional modest covering for nude figures in art, so it yields cover for many.

clue.text: Impressionist art? Flimsy, lacking initial power

indicators.note: lacking its initial means the word goes without its first letter

parts.note: papery means thin and flimsy like paper
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: An art critic sneers that Impressionist painting is insubstantial, without its early force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressionist' suggests Monet; here it is a mimic, someone who does impressions.
explanation.definitionFit: Apery is the practice of aping or mimicking others, the art of a performer who does impressions.

clue.text: Edible bulb in cold pile

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
to amass is to pile up

explanation.surface: An onion-like bulb is stored in a chilly heap.
explanation.definitionFit: Camass is a North American plant of the lily family whose bulbs were a staple food of Native peoples.

clue.text: Rising flatus with brownish outside? Its awful smell is misleading

indicators.note: the colour word sits outside, wrapping round the other piece

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: flatus is wind, air

explanation.surface: A rising puff of wind with a brown tinge has a smell worse than its reality.
explanation.definitionFit: The durian is a Southeast Asian fruit notorious for its foul smell but prized for its sweet, creamy taste.

clue.text: Treatment with chemical, foul spread in dividing portion

indicators.note: spread out, the letters are scattered into a different order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: a piece that divides another sits in the middle of it, splitting it in two

parts.note: a ration is a fixed portion
taken as written

explanation.surface: A treatment using some chemical has been spread over a split helping of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluorination is treatment with fluorine or a fluoride, for example adding it to drinking water.

clue.text: Controlling nasty smell around flower

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes round the second, enclosing it

parts.note: ming is a dialect word for a bad smell, as in minging
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: Someone is controlling a foul odour hanging about a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'flower' is often a river; here it is just a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastering something means getting it under control or command.

clue.text: I'll present perfect cleavage anatomically in part

indicators.note: the answer is only part of the following word, sitting inside it

parts.note: the letters sit in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: Someone promises to show off a low neckline, in anatomical terms.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleavage here is the mineralogist's term: a crystal splitting cleanly along planes, which the mineral does perfectly into thin sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Mica is a mineral famous for its perfect basal cleavage, peeling into very thin flexible sheets.

clue.text: Poet's rubbed out two thirds of scanning lines in set

indicators.note: only two thirds of the word stays, so its last third is cut away

parts.note: a raster is the set of scanning lines making up a television picture

explanation.surface: A poet has erased part of a line while scanning its metre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scanning lines' suggests checking a poem's metre; it is the screen's raster. Poet's marks a word found in Spenser.
explanation.definitionFit: Rast is Spenser's past participle of rase, to raze, so it means erased or destroyed.

clue.text: Small swelling turning up in an earlobe

indicators.note: turning round the whole assembled string means reading it backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, A

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the others, as if placed in them

parts.note: lap is an old word for the lobe of the ear
taken as written

explanation.surface: A little lump has appeared on someone's earlobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' applies to the whole assembly, not just to up: insert first, then read everything backwards. Lap is an old word for the lobe of the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A papula, or papule, is the medical term for a small raised pimple on the skin.

clue.text: Art forgery getting you reverse of short time

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read from its end back to its start

parts.note: curt means brief or short, especially in speech
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A faked painting lands you with the opposite of a brief spell, a long prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse of short time' reads like 'a long time'; in fact only short is reversed, and time is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Trucage is the faking of works of art, especially old pictures, a borrowing from French.

clue.text: Layer of humus not advantageous for fruit trees

parts.note: mor is a layer of acid humus formed on poor soil
U/S, unserviceable, is short for useless, so of no advantage

explanation.surface: Acid humus on the ground is no good for orchard trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Mor is a soil scientist's word; US is the abbreviation for unserviceable.
explanation.definitionFit: Morus is the botanical genus of the mulberries, trees grown for their fruit.

clue.text: Horse a sap crazily fed with soft potato

indicators.note: a thing fed with food has it put inside, so one piece goes within the other
something done crazily is wild and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, as anagram fodder
p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
aloo is the Hindi word for potato, familiar from Indian menus

explanation.surface: A foolish horse is being fed on a mushy potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft potato' looks like one mashed vegetable; soft is the musical piano sign, a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Appaloosa is a North American breed of horse with a distinctive spotted coat.

clue.text: I shoot from behind piercing one boozy light horseman

indicators.note: something piercing another thing goes into its body

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard, a boozy one

indicators.note: taken from behind, the words are read from the back end forwards

parts.note: to dart is to shoot along swiftly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gunman confesses to shooting a drunken cavalryman in the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A stradiot was a light cavalryman from the Balkans or Greece serving Venice in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.

clue.text: Bird offering sex behind bit of furniture

indicators.note: behind places that piece after the other one

parts.note: a pew is a bench in a church
it is a common slang word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A bird proposes some hanky-panky round the back of the furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: The pewit, also peewit, is the lapwing, named from its cry.

clue.text: Home of large bedroom furniture, finely wrought merchandise

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Hertfordshire town that gave its name to the Great Bed, a huge Elizabethan bed
second meaning: manufactured goods, especially pottery

explanation.walkthrough: The Great Bed of Ware, big enough for several couples and mentioned by Shakespeare, came from this town and is now in the Victoria and Albert Museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an English market town and articles for sale, as in silverware or earthenware.

clue.text: Line translated in successful exam result, easy

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, inside its letters

parts.note: a pass is the result of getting through an exam

indicators.note: something translated is rendered in a different form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A translated line in an exam that you passed comfortably was easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something painless causes no trouble or effort, so it is easy to do.

clue.text: Second at top of club producing meaningless utterance

indicators.note: in a down entry, being at the top puts that piece first

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a putter is a golf club used on the green

explanation.surface: A runner-up at the head of a club is reduced to babbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a society with a top member; it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A sputter is a burst of confused, spluttering speech that makes little sense.

clue.text: Gassy substance that's put out on paper

indicators.note: put out means upset or disturbed, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A gas is described as something published in print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as published; it is the anagram signal, as in disturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Propane is a flammable gaseous hydrocarbon used as bottled fuel.

clue.text: One presiding over golden age was model on vase

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece written on another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: an artist's model sits, or sat, for a portrait
an urn is a kind of vase

explanation.surface: Someone posed as a figure painted on a Greek vase.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman myth the god Saturn ruled during the golden age, an era of plenty and peace.

clue.text: Sausage? Individual leaves second tucking into minced pie

indicators.note: tucking into food puts it inside the eater, so one piece goes inside the other
minced meat is chopped up and mixed, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: when something leaves, it goes away and is no longer part of the word

parts.note: an individual is a single person
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A diner leaves the second course to eat a minced pie, wondering whether it holds a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' reads as a course of a meal; it is just its abbreviation, dropped from the individual.
explanation.definitionFit: Peperoni, usually pepperoni, is a spicy Italian dried sausage; the question mark admits it is one type among many.

clue.text: Small beers just after getting stuck into meat pastries

indicators.note: getting stuck into something means going right inside it

parts.note: pies are pastry cases filled with meat
on can mean immediately after, as in on arrival

explanation.surface: Half-pints straight after tucking into some meat pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small beers' sounds like trivia; here it is literal, small measures of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pony is a small glass, in Australia a small measure of beer, hence small beers.

clue.text: Aged hound lost glow

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an archaic word linked to the leash or lyam on which a hunting hound was led
second meaning: an archaic word for a gleam of light

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves carry an old-word marker, aged and lost, because both senses of this four-letter word are archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: In old English usage the word meant a gleam or shining light, and separately a leash for a hunting dog.

clue.text: Ace? It's enough when one's despatched for nothing

indicators.note: one thing despatched for another is sent off in exchange for it, a swap

parts.note: basta is Italian for enough, used as an exclamation in English
a means one
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A star player says enough is enough once a singleton is sent away for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The final A of the exclamation is replaced by O. The question mark warns that the ace is a card.
explanation.definitionFit: Basto is the ace of clubs in old card games such as ombre and quadrille, one particular ace.

clue.text: Daisy acting in long dress

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in the second, inside its letters

parts.note: a gown is a long formal dress
A is short for acting, as in an acting manager

explanation.surface: An actress called Daisy performs in a full-length frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy' looks like a woman's name, a performer in a costume; it is the definition, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Gowan is the Scots name for the daisy, especially the common white or yellow field flowers.

clue.text: Great Scot, filled with love, enterprising

indicators.note: a word filled with something has it put inside its letters

parts.note: gey is a Scots word for very or great
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A grand Scotsman, full of affection, is a go-getter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great Scot' reads as an exclamation; it is a Scots word for great.
explanation.definitionFit: Goey is an informal word for go-ahead or full of energy, someone with plenty of go.

clue.text: Musical part? One penned isn't too complicated

indicators.note: something penned is shut inside, enclosed by the other letters
complicated means tangled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped, as anagram fodder
a means one, as in a dozen

explanation.surface: A composer reassures that the song they wrote is not too hard to play.
explanation.walkthrough: The A goes among the letters of ISN'T TOO, and all eight are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostinato is a short phrase repeated persistently through a piece of music, one element of its texture.

clue.text: Wherein Malay sailors travel, characters regularly contributing to portolan

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of this word

explanation.surface: Seamen from Malaya sail by a portolan chart, picking out the navigation marks.
explanation.walkthrough: A portolan is a medieval sailing chart, a fitting source for a boat word.
explanation.definitionFit: A proa is a fast Malay sailing boat with an outrigger, the vessel in which the sailors travel.

clue.text: Windows, round, belonging to the kitchen, half blacked out

indicators.note: with half blacked out, only half of that word stays visible

parts.note: O is round in shape
culinary means relating to the kitchen or cooking

explanation.surface: The round kitchen windows have been half covered over.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half of CULINARY survives.
explanation.definitionFit: Oculi, plural of oculus, are round windows, especially in a church or a dome.

clue.text: Solid bit of fat Arab served in mugful

indicators.note: a drink served in a vessel sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a stein is a large beer mug
Ar is a dictionary abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: A lump of fat from an Arab dish is served in a mug.
explanation.definitionFit: Stearin is the solid part of a fat, a glyceride of stearic acid used in candles and soap.

clue.text: Brute's limping, hurt on hoof some time back

definitions.text: hurt on hoof some time back

indicators.note: a limping gait is uneven and disordered, so the letters fall out of place

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An animal is limping because its hoof was hurt a while ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some time back' marks the word as archaic: Spenser's form of surbated.
explanation.definitionFit: To surbate is to make the feet sore through walking; surbet is the old past participle, footsore or bruised.

clue.text: Tenderfoot, reverse of godsend

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or godsend

explanation.surface: For a beginner, things go the opposite way to a stroke of luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A noob is slang, mainly online, for a newcomer or novice, the same idea as a greenhorn.

clue.text: Aaron's converted and no longer bears name as part of old Jewish sect

definitions.text: name as part of old Jewish sect

indicators.note: something converted is changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped, as anagram fodder
ean is an archaic verb meaning to give birth, especially to lambs

explanation.surface: Aaron has converted and is no longer known by his name in an ancient Jewish sect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' flags an obsolete word: ean, to bring forth young, so bears in the sense of gives birth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nasoraeans were an early sect, Jewish in origin, whose name is still the self-designation of the Mandaeans' learned members.
